arguments.command:
cat > /workspace/project/README.md <<'EOF'
# CPU policy agent

`driver.py` is the collected JSON entry point. It validates the request
envelope and job schemas, accounts whole-request budgets, replays each job's
event stream and writes one JSON response.

- `syntax.py` — policy language tokenizer, recursive-descent parser and the
  declared per-string bounds (depth, complex rules, distinct non-match atoms,
  atom/path-service occurrence limits).
- `compiler/compiler.py` — compiles parsed rules into the canonical image:
  prefix trie for `match` atoms, KMP-style automata for the other atoms, lazy
  product search, bitset rule-formula evaluation, dead-residual elimination,
  Moore partition refinement and BFS renumbering from START in label order.
- `ebpf/helper.py` — the per-job replay agent: atomic image publication with
  pinned epochs, live units and cloned identities, multiplexed request
  contexts, transport packets with wire tags, file-mediated handoffs and exact
  resource accounting (every precondition is checked before any mutation).

Policy semantics: a sequence of services is allowed iff at least one allow rule
matches and no drop rule matches; `match` is exact equality, `startswith`,
`endswith` and `contains` are prefix, suffix and contiguous subsequence, and
boolean predicates combine over every finite sequence of registered services.
Images are the minimal complete language machines with the dead residual
removed; DENY=4294967295 marks dead transitions.

Kernel attachment and service deployment are outside this project.
EOF
cd /workspace && find . -name __pycache__ -type d | xargs rm -rf; ls -la project project/compiler project/ebpf; echo ---; du -sb project
